Cruz: This has reference to your 28 February 2012 letter requesting this Department's opinion/clarification on the following: 1. 2. 3. What is the effect of the exercise of the powers and performance of the duties and functions of the mayor by the Vice-Mayor on account of the indefinite leave of absence of the elected Mayor due to illness?; What functions remains with the elected Vice Mayor and what should be discharged by his successors in office? ; and To what extent can an acting Mayor and acting Vice Mayor exercise power with regard to personnel placements, more specifically with regard to confidential personnel in the office of the Mayor and the Vice Mayor? We shall answer you queries in seriatim, viz. : What is the effect of the exercise of the powers and performance of the duties and functions of the mayor by the Vice-Mayor on account of the indefinite leave of absence of the elected Mayor due to illness? The exercise of the powers and performance of the duties and functions of the Mayor by the Vice-Mayor during the time when the former is temporarily incapacitated to do the same creates a corresponding temporary vacancy in the latter's office during such contingency which may be paralleled to the case of Gamboa vs. Aguirre (G.R. No. 134213. July 20, 1999), which discusses the effects of vacancy in the office of the Governor, viz. : "It has been held that if a Mayor who is out of the country is considered "effectively absent', the Vice-Mayor should discharge the duties of the mayor during the latter's absence,LUl This doctrine should equally apply to the Vice-Governor since he is similarly situated as the Vice-Mayor. Althouqh it is difficult to lav down a definite rule as to what constitutes absence. yet this term should be reasonably construed to mean "effective" absence,115J that is. one that renders the officer concerned powerless. for the time beinq, to discharge the powers and preroqatives of his office.1151 There is no vacancy whenever the office is occupied bv a leqally. qualified incumbent. A sensu contrario. there is a vacancv when there is no person lawfully authorized to assume and exercise at present the duties of the office.1171By virtue of the foreqoinq definition, it can be said that the desiqnation, appointment or assumption of the Vice-Governor as the Actinq Governor creates a correspondinq temporary vacancy in the office of the Vice-Governor durinq such continqencv. Considerinq the silence of the law on the matter, the mode of succession rovided for ermanent vacancies under the new Code in the office of the Vice-Governor ma likewise be observed in the event of temporary vacancy occurrinq in the same office.11El This is so because in the eyes of the law, the office to which he was elected was left barren of a leqally qualified person to exercise the duties of the office of the Vice-Governor. Being the Acting Governor, the Vice-Governor cannot continue to simultaneously exercise the duties of the latter office, since the nature of the duties of the provincial Governor call for a full-time occupant to discharge Such is not only consistent with but also appears to be the clear rationale of the new Code wherein the policy of performing dual functions in both offices has already been abandoned. To repeat the creation of a temporary vacancv in the office of the Governor creates a correspondinq temporan/ vacancy in the office of the Vice-Governor whenever the latter acts as Governor bv virtue of such temporary vacancy. This event constitutes an "inability" on the part of the reqular presidinq officer (Vice Governor) to preside durinq the SP sessions. which thus calls for the operation of the remedy set in Article 49(b) of the Local Government Code - concerninq the election of a temporary presidinq officer. The continuity of the Actinq Governor's (Vice-Governor) powers as presidinq officer of the SP is suspended so lonq as he is in such capacity. Under Section 49(b), "(On the event of the

inability, of the r_ggular presidinq officer to preside at the sanqqunian session. the members present and gpnstitutinq a quorum shall elect from amonq themselves a temporary presidinq officer. "120) (Emphasis and underscoring, ours] However, the Vice-Mayor cannot simultaneously perform the functions and duties in both the offices of the Mayor and Vice-Mayor because it would intermingle two (2) separate powers, i.e., executive and legislative, which has been delineated and vested by law to two (2) separate offices, to provide a system of checks and balances thereby ensuring a better delivery of public service. What functions remains with the elected Vice Mayor and what should be discharged by his successors in office? While acting as Acting Mayor, the elected Vice Mayor is legally deprived to exercise the functions appurtenant to his office by reason of the principle of separation of powers. This would now lead to the application of the case of Menzon vs. Petilla (G.R. No. 90762. May 20, 1991), where the Supreme Court ruled that to obviate the dilemma resulting from an interregnum created by the temporary vacancy in the Office of the Vice Governor, there being no provision of law governing the mode of succession in case of a temporary vacancy in said office, the mode of succession for permanent vacancy in the Office of the Vice Governor may be analogously applied. Accordingly, the highest ranking sanggunian member shall now assume temporarily as Acting Vice Mayor. However, while the highest ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member, as Acting Vice Mayor, can perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office of the Vice Mayor, the —Presiding Officership function is not automatically given to him in view of the ruling of the Supreme Court in the case of Gamboa vs. Aguirre stating that the issue of Presiding Officership in this kind of situation shall be resolved by applying Section 49 (b) of the Local Government Code, in which case, the majority of those present members there being a quorum shall elect from among themselves the temporary Presiding Officer for that session. To what extent can an acting Mayor and acting Vice Mayor exercise power with regard to personnel placements, more specifically with regard to confidential personnel in the office of the Mayor and the Vice Mayor? Under Section 46 (a) of the Code, the Vice Mayor acting as Acting Mayor can perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office of the Mayor, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Thus, if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days, the Acting Mayor may already proceed to exercise such functions so as not to impair the delivery of vital public services. The Acting Mayor's power to appoint, suspend or dismiss applies without any distinction, subject to the promulgated rules and regulations of the Civil Service Commission. On the other hand, the Acting Vice-Mayor was not granted by the Code the same power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees. Hence, he is precluded from the exercise of such powers. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, JESU . DQQUE IV Dire r 111 D
